<issue>
--purge-old deletes a mirrored file when the connection drops before the response
A re-fetch whose connection closes before any response arrives leaves the mirrored copy untouched: nothing is written, nothing is cached. The file never reaches `hts-cache/new.lst` either, so the end-of-session purge (`opt->delete_old`, on by default) removes it as if it had vanished from the site.

Same data-loss family as #562, which was closed for the short-`Content-Length` path. A connection that dies before the status line takes a different route into `back_finalize()` and still reproduces on master (f72e7eb).

Repro, against a local server that serves `/reset.bin` in full on the first fetch and, on every later fetch, closes the connection without answering:

1. `httrack --retries=2 -O out http://127.0.0.1:PORT/index.html` mirrors index.html, ok.bin and reset.bin.
2. `httrack --retries=2 --update -O out ...`: all three attempts at reset.bin fail, and the pass-1 bytes sit on disk untouched for the whole crawl.
3. End of session: old.lst lists reset.bin, new.lst does not, and the purge deletes it. The same run with `--purge-old=0` keeps the file, which pins the mechanism.

Found while working on #714 (`--changes`), which computes the same old.lst-minus-new.lst set. The report side now refuses to call such a file gone; the deletion is untouched.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (httrack), find back_finalize() in src/htsback.c and how #562 fix handled short Content-Length (look for code that marks file as 'kept'/ adds to new.lst / cache entry for unchanged files, e.g. in htscore.c or htsback.c). Report the relevant code snippets with line numbers: the #562 fix, and the path in back_finalize for a connection that closes before status line (statuscode STATUSCODE_CONNERROR / -1 etc, 'Connection reset' / 'Empty reply'). Show how the file would get into new.lst (cache_wr / 'hts-cache/new.lst' writing, e.g. filenote / structcheck).

content.content: {"summary":"The #562 fix lives in back_finalize()'s incomplete-transfer branch: when the body is shorter than Content-Length, it keeps the existing local copy by calling filenote(), which writes it into new.lst. A connection that closes before the status line gets statuscode -1/-4 and does not reach that branch, so it does not get a filenote() from there. I did not trace the full path for that case, so treat that part as partial.","findings":["src/htsback.c:640-655: back_finalize() 'Don't store broken files' gate: if totalsize>=0 && statuscode>0 && size!=totalsize && !opt->tolerant, it logs 'incomplete transfer ... will be retried', calls back_finalize_backup(HTS_FALSE) (restore previous copy), then if fexist_utf8(url_sav) calls filenote(&opt->state.strc, url_sav, NULL), returns -1. The #562 comment at 649-650 says the kept copy must be in new.lst or the update purge deletes it.","src/htscore.c:2992-3004: filenote() appends '[savename]' to strc->lst (new.lst) via hts_savename_listed + fprintf + fflush; it is a no-op when strc->lst is NULL.","src/htscore.c:2155-2164: the update purge computes old.lst minus new.lst; files absent from new.lst are deleted, which is why the #562 filenote matters.","src/htsback.c:657-660: the same gate is also what keeps partial files out of the cache (no cache write on this path).","src/htsback.c:~740-775: the re-compression path also calls filenote() on success (743) and on failed decode (771-775, with comment 'failed decode keeps the previously-mirrored copy').","src/htsback.c:~3727-3863 and 4054: other filenote() calls for 206 resume and non-HTML resume paths keep partial files listed.","Gate at src/htsback.c ~line 645 (back[p].r.statuscode > 0) means a -1/-4 error does not enter the incomplete-transfer branch, so no filenote() is issued from back_finalize for that case.","src/htsbasenet.h:142-145: STATUSCODE_INVALID=-1, TIMEOUT=-2, SLOW=-3, CONNERROR=-4.","src/htsback.c:4201-4215: r.empty response path calls back_maydeletehttp, sets STATUS_READY, malloc 2-byte empty adr, then back_finalize() if !locked.","src/htsback.c:4325-4331: connect-fallback exhaustion sets statuscode=STATUSCODE_CONNERROR and msg 'Connect Error', then STATUS_READY.","src/htsback.c:4080-4090 (approx): the 'Connection reset / closed before status line' handling was NOT located in the preloaded output (it was truncated); I did not verify where that sets statuscode."],"confidence":0.6}

Print lines from ~930 to the function's end.
